title: Dispatcher personas: competing strategies that order, separate, chain and cut cards
summary: A new persona role decides which Ready card starts when, what runs in parallel and what is chained, and for packaging personas how findings are cut into cards. Dispatcher personas name pure, versioned strategies evaluated in the decision library (model-free in the hot path); one is live per project, the others run in shadow on the same facts. Five starter personas: Queue keeper (today's order), Area warden (one card per forecast module), Surveyor (file overlap), Historian (learns from a new conflict ledger with partner attribution), Packer (packages and chains overlapping findings before the start). Today's local pick-gate derives a scope from prompt paths but compares only with running cards, and the remote claim that ran the 17 November wave applies no scope rule. A replay of the 57 playthrough cards of that wave, rebuilt from git, matches history (20 replayed against 21 observed cards needing a develop sync) and shows the Area warden on forecast modules cutting that to 7 with instant integration; with an integration lag a running-only check leaves 29 to 35 cards for every strategy, an in-flight check 12 to 15. The keyword areas of the prompt enrichment are too coarse (53 of 55 cards tagged frontend, pair precision 0.23). Criteria combine into one weighted value with a parallelism gate, because a plain sum ranks a nearly sequential warden first. Ten decisions with recommendations, character sheet and review page mockups, and twelve slices whose area separation is carried entirely by dependsOn edges.

openDecisions.title: Form of a dispatcher
openDecisions.question: Is a dispatcher a model session, a pure strategy chosen by a persona, or a project setting?

options.A: Model session that orders the lane
options.B: Persona names a pure strategy in the decision library

openDecisions.recommendation: B. Persona names a pure strategy in the decision library
openDecisions.rationale: Decisions are frequent and must be replayable, explainable and token-free; sessions only write recut texts and reports.

openDecisions.title: Where the order lives
openDecisions.question: Does the dispatcher write the lane order or its own plan?

options.B: Separate dispatch plan read by the pick-gate; pins and urgent stay hard

openDecisions.recommendation: B. Separate dispatch plan read by the pick-gate; pins and urgent stay hard
openDecisions.rationale: Owner drags keep their meaning and plans stay comparable between personas.

openDecisions.title: Rights and tiers
openDecisions.question: Which dispatcher actions are T1 and which need an explicit T2 grant?

options.B: Bounded T1 (order, hold at most 24 h, own edges, exclusive, bounded recut); T2 for every bypass

openDecisions.recommendation: B. Bounded T1 (order, hold at most 24 h, own edges, exclusive, bounded recut); T2 for every bypass
openDecisions.rationale: Follows the persona team tiers; nothing that bypasses a check runs on a standing grant.

openDecisions.title: Touch forecast
openDecisions.question: What tells a dispatcher which files a card will touch?

options.A: Keyword areas from the prompt enrichment
options.B: Shared model-free forecast: cited paths, co-change expansion, module map, confidence; real files recorded

openDecisions.recommendation: B. Shared model-free forecast: cited paths, co-change expansion, module map, confidence; real files recorded
openDecisions.rationale: Pair F1 0.52 to 0.56 at zero tokens against 0.37 for keyword areas; a model-assisted forecast stays a persona option.

openDecisions.title: Conflict record
openDecisions.question: How are conflicts recorded so that they can be attributed and learned from?

options.A: Latest report per card, as today
options.B: Append-only ledger with partner attribution and admitting decisions, backfilled for 30 days

openDecisions.recommendation: B. Append-only ledger with partner attribution and admitting decisions, backfilled for 30 days
openDecisions.rationale: Without partner and decision a conflict cannot be charged to a dispatcher.

openDecisions.title: Competition order
openDecisions.question: In which order do personas compete?

options.B: Replay, then shadow, then alternating live by wave window per project, behind a guard

openDecisions.recommendation: B. Replay, then shadow, then alternating live by wave window per project, behind a guard
openDecisions.rationale: Cheap and safe first; real tokens and behaviour only for the top two.

openDecisions.title: Criteria and value
openDecisions.question: How do the criteria combine into one value?

options.B: Weighted sum with min-max scores and a parallelism gate at 0.8; default weights 30, 25, 10, 10, 10, 5, 5, 5

openDecisions.recommendation: B. Weighted sum with min-max scores and a parallelism gate at 0.8; default weights 30, 25, 10, 10, 10, 5, 5, 5
openDecisions.rationale: A plain sum ranks a nearly sequential warden first (81); the gate drops it to 45.

openDecisions.title: Recut and source cut
openDecisions.question: Who may recut cards, and what must sources provide?

options.B: Packer recuts unstarted automated-source cards with undo; sources emit wave id and cited paths; size from a source prior

openDecisions.recommendation: B. Packer recuts unstarted automated-source cards with undo; sources emit wave id and cited paths; size from a source prior
openDecisions.rationale: Waves of 57 cards arrive in one minute; size is not predictable from text (r at most 0.12), so a source prior bounds packages.

openDecisions.title: First live persona
openDecisions.question: Which persona takes the live lease first?

options.B: Area warden on forecast modules after its shadow gate; Packer in shadow with proposals

openDecisions.recommendation: B. Area warden on forecast modules after its shadow gate; Packer in shadow with proposals
openDecisions.rationale: Most robust in the replay: first or tied first in three of four runs and two points behind the Packer in the base run; model-free, needs no recut rights.

openDecisions.title: Exposure window of the overlap check
openDecisions.question: Which cards does the pick-gate compare a candidate with?

options.B: Every in-flight card of the project, from start to integration, on the local pickup and the remote claim
options.C: In flight only between cards of one source wave

openDecisions.recommendation: B. Every in-flight card of the project, from start to integration, on the local pickup and the remote claim
openDecisions.rationale: With an integration lag of one card duration a running-only check leaves 29 to 35 of 57 cards needing a sync under every strategy; in flight the forecast personas reach 12 to 15. The slot cost is accepted because efficiency comes before lead time.

# DS-0 · Overlap check on both claim paths over the exposure window

Source: `docs/dispatcher-personas/index.html` (AGT-3974), replay data and script in `docs/dispatcher-personas/replay/`. Read AGENTS.md, docs/system/contracts/orchestration-decisions.md and `docs/persona-team/index.html` (persona team, capability addendum) first. Each Dossier recommendation (DS-D1 to DS-D10) is the working decision unless a recorded operator decision selects another option; record the option implemented in the results status. Orchestration rules live only in `orchestration-decisions/` as pure policies; hosts collect facts and apply returned decisions. Workspace data only through the application API; git stays with the platform. One bounded slice; no em dashes in text.

**Area:** `backend/Features/Runner/` (`ProjectRunner` admission facts, `ActiveRuns` comparison set, `PredictParallelism` moved to a shared helper), `backend/Features/Tasks/LeaseEndpoints.cs` (remote claim), `backend/Shared/Models/ProjectSettings.cs` (one setting)

## Why
The Dossier section Exposure window shows that a card stays exposed from its start until it integrates, while today's local pick-gate compares a candidate only with running cards, and the remote claim (`LeaseEndpoints`, which ran the 17 November wave) applies no scope rule at all. Decision DS-D10, recommended option B.

## Deliver
1. Move `ProjectRunner.PredictParallelism` and `ScopePathRegex` into a shared helper with byte-identical behaviour (parent directory of every named `backend/`, `frontend/`, `src/`, `docs/`, `tools/` path in title and `prompt.md`, at most 24; none means unknown scope).
2. Project setting `dispatch.overlapWindow`: `running` (today's local behaviour) or `in-flight` (default). In `in-flight`, the comparison set is every card of the project that has started a coding run and has not integrated yet: Progress, the review lanes, cards waiting for the batch gate or integration, and queued merge rounds. Their scopes come from the same helper.
3. The remote claim calls `ParallelSlotPolicy.Decide` for each candidate in `LaneSortApplier.PickupOrder` against that comparison set (leased running cards plus, in `in-flight`, the other in-flight cards) and skips a conflicting candidate with a `parallel-conflict` pickup skip, as the local pickup does.
4. Every serialize names the window, the conflicting card and the shared prefix in the pickup skip and the runner log, so DS-4 and DS-7 can measure over-serialization later.
5. Exclusive cards keep blocking only while running; unknown scope stays optimistic. No change to lane order.

Record in the results status which window is the default and how many serializes the first day produced.
